items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...It reminds me of Frank Wess who would play tenor parts on his alto with Basie...

ctx.x: And so he arranged the wrong “Ave Maria.” Okay? So now there’s a lot of commotion in there. So they decide to record this version of “Ave Maria.” And Gladys Knight is in there so they figure out what key she should do it in so now there’s five minutes left in the session. There’s time for one take. And the conductor walks in and he says, “‘Ave Maria’ down a fourth. One-two-three-four.” And that’s the one that’s on the record. Everybody transposed it instantaneously.

Wow. I’m speechless. You know for — I play alto so I’m pretty good at you know, up a minor third from concert, etcetera, or you know tenor down, but that’s really something. It reminds me of Frank Wess who would play tenor parts on his alto with Basie ‘cause he was too lazy to pick up the other horn or whatever, and he just did that.

Well I can do that, I can read an alto part on tenor and vice versa, tenor part on alto. I can read a trumpet part on the trombone. I can read a baritone part — I can do that too. Being an arranger you know I can read any horn part on any other, yeah, just because I’ve been doing it so long.
